data.name: Developer Update - August 2026
data.body: Here’s everything that happened with Supabase in the last month: ## Supabase Select SF 2026 Supabase Select returns to San Francisco on October 2, a curated day of talks, feature deep dives, and more activations. Tickets are now available by application. [Get your ticket →](https://select.supabase.com/) ## Supabase Pipelines is now in public alpha Supabase Pipelines streams Postgres changes to BigQuery in near real time, a managed CDC service you configure in the Dashboard, now available on all paid plans. [Read the blog →](https://supabase.com/blog/supabase-pipelines-public-alpha) ## Sign in with ChatGPT is now in beta !chatgpt.png Sign in to Supabase with your ChatGPT account, or connect Supabase to ChatGPT on desktop, web, and mobile through the ChatGPT plugins directory. [Read the blog →](https://supabase.com/blog/sign-in-with-chatgpt-beta) ## Unified Logs is now in open beta Unified Logs gives you one searchable view across every Supabase service, with live tail, filtering, and a timeline. [Read the blog →](https://supabase.com/blog/unified-logs-open-beta) ## Observability for every project with Grafana Cloud Connect any Supabase project to Grafana Cloud in one click for a pre-built dashboard, alerting, and metrics, available on every plan including Free. [Read the blog →](https://supabase.com/blog/observability-for-every-supabase-project-with-grafana-cloud) ## Introducing Supabase Evals Supabase Evals is now open source, a benchmark that runs AI coding agents like Claude Code and Codex against real Supabase tasks and publishes the scores. [Read the blog →](https://supabase.com/blog/introducing-supabase-evals) ## Searchable field-level encryption with CipherStash CipherStash adds field-level encryption to Supabase with queryable ciphertext, zero-knowledge key management, and no schema changes. [Read the blog →](https://supabase.com/blog/searchable-field-level-encryption-with-cipherstash) ## Quick Product Announcements - The Edge Functions overview page now shows each function's error rates, execution time, and CPU and memory use in one place. [[Twitter](https://x.com/supabase/status/2080669559967657995)] - Extension version pinning is deprecated: from August 5, an explicit version in `CREATE` or `ALTER EXTENSION` is ignored and the default version installs with a warning. [[Changelog](https://supabase.com/changelog/extension-version-pinning-ignored)] - The Management API `analytics/endpoints/logs.all` endpoint is migrating to the new logs endpoint, so update any clients that query project logs. [[Changelog](https://supabase.com/changelog/48235-migration-of-supabase-management-api-logs-all-analytics-endpoint-to-logs-endpoint)] - Supabase now blocks all changes to the `realtime` schema: creating, altering, or dropping objects fails with a permission error, and RLS policies on `realtime.messages` keep working. [[Changelog](https://supabase.com/changelog/realtime-schema-locked-down-against-modification)] ## Made with Supabase - byTheLab GEO Score measures how visible your brand is across AI search engines like ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, and Gemini, and returns a score in about 30 seconds. [[Website](https://geo.bythelab.xyz/)] - Huevsite is a profile platform where indie builders show their projects, code, and stack and earn a Builder Score to get discovered. [[Website](https://huevsite.io/)] - TripMaster keeps a group trip's flights, stays, and tickets on one shared timeline, texts the group when a gate or time changes, and connects to ChatGPT or Claude to fill in the plan. [[Website](https://www.tripmaster.dev/)] - FutureNerds is a management platform for Montessori schools that tracks each child's progress, keeps parents updated, and runs day-to-day school operations. [[Website](https://www.futurenerds.dev/)] ## Community Highlights - A no-code introduction to Supabase covering how the database, auth, and free tier work for builders who are not writing backend code. [[Read](https://www.whalesync.com/blog/no-coder-guide-to-supabase)] - A production-readiness review of Supabase, covering the Row Level Security policy fix that gives more than 100x improvement on large tables. [[Read](https://unicoconnect.com/blogs/is-supabase-production-ready)] - A step-by-step Supabase starter guide covering migrations, typed clients, Row Level Security, auth, and a production-safe local workflow. [[Read](https://dopebase.com/blog/getting-started-supabase-comprehensive-tutorial)] - A production Row Level Security walkthrough covering multi-tenant isolation, role-based access patterns, policy performance, and the mistakes that silently break apps. [[Read](https://designrevision.com/blog/supabase-row-level-security)] - A founder's assessment of why Postgres-based backends are winning for small teams, including an honest list of where Supabase is not the right pick. [[Read](https://blog.mean.ceo/supabase-news-july-2026/)]

commit.message:
refactor(studio): migrate update_opt_in_level to a tool contract (#52081)

## Problem

`update_opt_in_level` is the last local assistant tool not on the tool
contract pattern. Its input schema is built for each request: a
transform captures the org's opt-in level, stamps `levelWhenAsked`, and
drops `requiredLevel` when the org already has it. The SDK stores that
parsed value, and the approval card reads it before the tool runs. A
contract has one static `inputSchema`, so this didn't fit.

Separately, `pages/api/ai/sql/policy.ts` passes every assistant tool to
a one-shot `generateText` and only removes `update_opt_in_level`. Any
tool with `needsApproval` (`execute_sql`, `deploy_edge_function`, the
notebook mutation and run tools) stops the step loop with no result, so
`output` is never set and the route returns a 500.

## Solution

- `ToolContract` gains an optional `createInputSchema(ctx)`.
`toolFromContract` parses with it when present. `inputSchema` stays the
shape stored on the message, which is what history replay and the client
parse.
- `update_opt_in_level` moves to `update-opt-in-level.ts` and
`update-opt-in-level.server.ts`:
- The per-request transform becomes `createInputSchema`; the stored
shape is `inputSchema`.
- The output schema moves out of `OptInRequest.tsx` into the contract;
`toModelOutput` returns it unchanged, since it only contains level
names.
- `minOptInLevel: null` and `needsApproval: true`, as before. It uses
plain `toolFromContract`, since it promotes no SQL.
- Registered in `TOOL_CONTRACTS`, removed from `TOOL_CATEGORY_MAP`.
`getOptInTools` still registers it on platform at every level.
- `Message.Parts.tsx`, `OptInRequest.tsx`, and `evals/opt-in-replay.ts`
use the contract's schemas; the old schemas in `tool-filter.ts` and
`studio-tools.ts` are removed.
- `ToolContext.aiOptInLevel` is now required. The `'schema'` defaults in
`toolFromContract`, `execute-sql.server.ts`, and
`run-notebook.server.ts` are gone, and every caller passes the real
level. The eval mocks pin the mocked studio tools to `'schema'` so eval
results don't shift.
- New `withoutApprovalTools(tools)` in `tool-filter.ts` drops any tool
whose `needsApproval` is set (including a function, and privacy-stubbed
tools). `policy.ts` uses it instead of deleting one tool.

## Behavior changes

- Replayed `update_opt_in_level` outputs are validated against the
output schema and dropped if invalid (previously unchecked).
- The policy generator no longer offers approval-gated tools to the
model.

## Testing

- New `update-opt-in-level.test.ts` (transform, per-request schema,
execute at a new level, replay) and `tool-from-contract.test.ts`
(`createInputSchema` used when present and receives the context).
- `withoutApprovalTools` tests in `tool-filter.test.ts`.
- `pnpm exec vitest run lib/ai components/ui/AIAssistantPanel evals`
passes in `apps/studio`.

+import type { ToolUIPart } from 'ai'
+import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest'
+import { z } from 'zod'
+
+import { sanitizeContractPart } from './registry'
+import { contract } from './update-opt-in-level'
+import { createTool } from './update-opt-in-level.server'
+
+const executeOptions = { toolCallId: 'test', messages: [], context: {} }
+
+describe('update_opt_in_level contract', () => {
+  it.each([
+    ['schema_and_log_and_data', 'schema', undefined],
+    ['schema', 'schema', undefined],
+    ['schema', 'schema_and_log', 'schema_and_log'],
+    ['schema', undefined, undefined],
+  ] as const)('at level %s, requested %s is stored as %s', (level, requested, stored) => {
+    const parsed = contract
+      .createInputSchema({ aiOptInLevel: level })
+      .parse({ requiredLevel: requested })
+    expect(parsed).toEqual({ levelWhenAsked: level, requiredLevel: stored })
+  })
+
+  it('builds the tool with the per-request input schema', () => {
+    const tool = createTool({ aiOptInLevel: 'schema_and_log_and_data' })
+    expect(tool.inputSchema).not.toBe(contract.inputSchema)
+    const parsed = (tool.inputSchema as z.ZodType).parse({ requiredLevel: 'schema' })
+    expect(parsed).toEqual({ levelWhenAsked: 'schema_and_log_and_data' })
+  })
+
+  it.each([
+    ['schema', 'schema_and_log_and_data', false],
+    ['schema_and_log_and_data', 'schema', true],
+    ['schema', 'schema', true],
+    ['schema', undefined, undefined],
+  ] as const)(
+    'level %s after approval, stored required %s gives sufficient %s',
+    async (level, requiredLevel, sufficient) => {
+      const tool = createTool({ aiOptInLevel: level })
+      if (!tool.execute) throw new Error('execute is undefined')
+
+      const result = await tool.execute({ levelWhenAsked: 'schema', requiredLevel }, executeOptions)
+
+      expect(tool.needsApproval).toBe(true)
+      expect(result).toMatchObject({
+        levelAfterReview: level,
+        ...(sufficient !== undefined && { sufficient }),
+      })
+      if (sufficient === false) expect(result).toHaveProperty('status')
+      else expect(result).not.toHaveProperty('status')
+    }
+  )
+
+  describe('sanitizeContractPart', () => {
+    const part = {
+      type: 'tool-update_opt_in_level',
+      toolCallId: 'call-1',
+      state: 'output-available',
+      input: {},
+      output: { levelAfterReview: 'schema_and_log', sufficient: true },
+    } as ToolUIPart
+
+    it('round-trips a valid output', () => {
+      expect(sanitizeContractPart(part, 'schema')?.output).toEqual(part.output)
+    })
+
+    it('drops an invalid output', () => {
+      const invalid = { ...part, output: { levelAfterReview: 'everything' } } as ToolUIPart
+      expect(sanitizeContractPart(invalid, 'schema')?.output).toBe(undefined)
+    })
+  })
+})

+import { z } from 'zod'
+
+import type { ToolContract } from './types'
+import { isOptInLevelAtLeast, optInLevelSchema } from '@/lib/ai/opt-in-level'
+
+/** What the model sends. */
+const modelInputSchema = z.object({
+  requiredLevel: z
+    .enum(['schema', 'schema_and_log', 'schema_and_log_and_data'])
+    .optional()
+    .describe(
+      'The lowest opt-in level that unlocks what you need: `schema` for table and column metadata, `schema_and_log` for logs, `schema_and_log_and_data` for query results. Omit it when the user just wants to review or change the setting, for example to lower it.'
+    ),
+})
+
+/**
+ * Input as stored on the message. `levelWhenAsked` is the org's level when the call was made.
+ * Optional because older chats may lack it.
+ */
+const storedInputSchema = modelInputSchema.extend({
+  levelWhenAsked: optInLevelSchema.optional(),
+})
+
+type StoredInput = z.infer<typeof storedInputSchema>
+
+const outputSchema = z.object({
+  levelAfterReview: optInLevelSchema,
+  sufficient: z.boolean().optional(),
+  status: z.string().optional(),
+})
+
+type Output = z.infer<typeof outputSchema>
+
+export const contract = {
+  name: 'update_opt_in_level',
+  description:
+    'Asks the user to review or change the organization-wide AI opt-in level. Call it with `requiredLevel` when a tool needs a higher level than the organization has or you need to read query results. Call it without `requiredLevel` whenever the user asks to change the setting, including lowering it. Do not call it again in the same chat after the user skipped it unless they ask.',
+  inputSchema: storedInputSchema,
+  createInputSchema: ({ aiOptInLevel }) =>
+    modelInputSchema.transform(({ requiredLevel }) => ({
+      levelWhenAsked: aiOptInLevel,
+      ...(requiredLevel && !isOptInLevelAtLeast(aiOptInLevel, requiredLevel) && { requiredLevel }),
+    })),
+  outputSchema,
+  minOptInLevel: null,
+  needsApproval: true,
+  toModelOutput: (output) => output,
+} as const satisfies ToolContract<StoredInput, Output>
